title: Protocol
description: Schema root: both wire directions under one document so the shared `$defs` (`FsResult`, `ProcResult`, `EntrypointEvent`, …) are emitted once and the generated clients reference a single definition set.

AgentProfile.description:
Profile baked into an mvm guest image. Determines the set of vsock verbs the guest agent's dispatcher will accept; dev-only verbs (`Exec`, `ConsoleOpen`, `ProcStart`, `RunCode`, filesystem RPC, port forwarding) are rejected pre-handler when the image declares `SealedProd`.

**Source of truth.** The profile is declared by the image config — `/etc/mvm/security.json` on a sealed-prod image lives on a dm-verity rootfs (ADR-002 §W3), so the value cannot be widened at runtime: any modification breaks the verity hash and the kernel panics in `mvm-verity-init` before userspace. The loader treats absence of the policy file as an unprovisioned dev image (`SecurityPolicy::dev_defaults`).

**Builder uses a different protocol.** `mvm-builder-agent`'s wire type is `HostVmRequest`, not `GuestRequest`; the `Builder` profile is reserved for any future `GuestRequest` variant that only makes sense during a build. No current variant is `BuilderOnly`, so the value is wire-stable but unused for the tenant agent today.

oneOf.description: Hardened production guest. Only ADR-002 production-safe verbs pass the dispatcher gate.
Development guest. Adds shell exec, process RPC, filesystem RPC, console, port forwarding, and `RunCode`.
Builder-VM agent. Reserved for `BuilderOnly`-classified verbs when the builder protocol moves to `GuestRequest`; today the builder agent speaks `HostVmRequest` exclusively.

BackpressureReason.description:
Why a streaming or queued operation is currently throttled.

Closed enum: every reason is named, and drift between host and guest fails the serde `deny_unknown_fields`-equivalent path (variants must match). Detail strings carried alongside this enum in W4 are bounded and redacted — never argv / env / stdin / stdout / stderr / filesystem paths.

oneOf.description: Host could not reach the guest agent within the configured grace period. Typically resolves on the next probe.
One or more integration readiness probes are still pending.

pending.description: Names of services whose readiness scripts have not yet reported success. Echoed verbatim — never user payload.

oneOf.description: The host is not draining the data-plane stream fast enough, so the guest is holding back to honor the frame cap.
Bounded input ring is saturated. The producer must wait.
A chunked artifact transfer is paused (typically host disk pressure or quota).
The shared builder VM is occupied by another build; this run is queued behind it.

BootTimingReport.description:
Per-phase monotonic boot timings in milliseconds since the agent process started.

Plan 76 Phase 4 fills in the full per-phase set. Phase 2 wires `agent_started_ms`, `vsock_bound_ms`, `first_accept_ms`, and `entrypoint_ready_ms` so callers can already display the cold-path timing breakdown. Fields populated by Phase 4 (`warm_pool_ready_ms`, `integrations_ready_ms`, `probes_ready_ms`) stay `None` for now.

agent_started_ms.description: Milliseconds from agent process start to vsock bind/listen. Always present once the agent has bound — this number is the dominant signal for early-readiness regressions.

entrypoint_ready_ms.description: Milliseconds from agent start to `entrypoint = Ready` (or `Failed`). `None` while still `Starting`.

first_accept_ms.description: Milliseconds from agent start to the first accepted host connection. `None` until the first `accept()` returns.

integrations_ready_ms.description: Filled in by Phase 4. `None` for now.

probes_ready_ms.description: Filled in by Phase 4. `None` for now.

vsock_bound_ms.description: Milliseconds from agent start to a successful `bind+listen` pair on the control port. Same anchor as `agent_started_ms` today; reserved for diverging if a future Phase 4 refactor splits "process started" from "socket created".

warm_pool_ready_ms.description: Filled in by Phase 4. `None` for now.

ComponentState.description:
State of a single guest subsystem during boot.

`Disabled` is distinct from `Ready` — a missing optional subsystem (no integrations declared, no warm pool configured, no probes registered) reports `Disabled`, while a present-and-warmed subsystem reports `Ready`. This lets the host UX distinguish "the workload doesn't use X" from "X is still warming".

`Default` is `Disabled` — the most-conservative semantically correct value (= "this subsystem isn't configured"). Lets constructors of `ReadinessReport` use `..Default::default()` to elide subsystems they don't care about in tests / fixtures.

oneOf.description: Subsystem is not configured for this image (no policy → no state machine to advance). Wire-stable distinct from `Ready`.
Subsystem is initializing in the background.
Subsystem is up and accepting work.
Subsystem failed to initialize. `message` is a short human- readable reason; no secrets / paths beyond what the host already knows.

message.description: Short human-readable failure reason. Stable enough for an operator to recognise, not a structured cause — pair with stderr logs for diagnosis.

EntrypointEvent.description:
One event in the streaming response of a `RunEntrypoint` call. ADR-007 / plan 41 W1.

`Stdout` / `Stderr` carry bytes from the wrapper's respective streams. `Exit` and `Error` are terminal — they end the response stream for one call. The agent emits exactly one terminal event per call.

v1 buffers each stream fully before sending one `Stdout` and one `Stderr` event (sizes bounded by agent caps). v2 may chunk progressively without changing the type or the protocol shape: the host already reads frames in a loop until terminal.

oneOf.description: Bytes from the wrapper's stdout.
Bytes from the wrapper's stderr.

One control-channel record from the wrapper's fd-3 (Plan-0010 §B4 / phase 4 of the upstream-mvm coordination work in `specs/upstream-mvm-prompt.md`).

fd-3 is a separate stream the wrapper writes structured records to — error envelopes, captured logs when capture is on, etc. — that user code cannot spoof by writing to stderr. stdout / stderr keep streaming user-visible bytes verbatim.

The on-the-fd-3-wire frame format is:

```text header_len:  u32 LE   (4 bytes; max 64 KiB) header_json: bytes    (header_len bytes; UTF-8 JSON object) payload_len: u32 LE   (4 bytes; max bounded by call caps) payload:     bytes    (payload_len bytes; opaque) ```

`header_json` is a JSON object with at minimum `{"kind": "<str>"}`. The agent re-emits the header as `header_json: String` and the payload bytes as `payload: Vec<u8>` — no agent-side parsing beyond the framing. The host (`mvmctl invoke` and downstream SDKs) decides what to do with each record kind.

**Wiring status (phase 4a):** the variant ships ahead of any emitter. Agents at this version do not yet open fd-3 in the child or emit `Control` events; phase 4b lands fd-3 wiring in the cold path (`execute()`), phase 4c in the warm-process pool, and the wrapper templates flip from stderr-envelope to fd-3-envelope at the same time. Hosts that see a `Control` event must already know how to consume it, so this variant is added eagerly to keep host/guest deserializers in lockstep.

header_json.description: JSON-encoded record header (deserialized by the host into a kind-specific struct). Agent does not parse beyond UTF-8 validation.

payload.description: Opaque per-record payload. Empty for envelope-style records; used for raw bytes on log-style records.

oneOf.description: Wrapper exited with the given code. Terminal.
Agent-side condition that prevented or interrupted the call (cap breach, timeout, busy session, missing entrypoint, crashed wrapper, internal failure). Terminal.

FsChange.description: A single filesystem change detected since boot.

path.description: Path relative to the filesystem root.

size.description: File size in bytes (0 for deleted files).

kind.description: File type. `Other` covers sockets, FIFOs, devices.

name.description: Bare entry name (no leading directory component).

size.description: Size in bytes, or `0` for non-files.

FsEntryKind.description: Type of a filesystem entry returned by `FsList` / `FsStat`.

FsErrorKind.description: Class of error returned in `FsResult::Error`. Closed enum so the host can branch on `kind` without parsing message text.

oneOf.description: Path was rejected by the agent's policy (deny-list, canonicalization failed, symlink crossed the deny-list).
Path doesn't exist.
Caller does not have permission for this op (uid 901 EPERM).
Target already exists where the verb required absence.
Size / count cap exceeded (e.g. `length > 16 MiB`, `recursive` walk would exceed cap).
Tried to rename across filesystems (`EXDEV`).
`recursive=false` on a non-empty directory.
Underlying I/O error (look at `message` for detail).
Path canonicalization succeeded but produced a path the agent refuses to operate on (e.g. `/proc/self`).
Other / unclassified.

FsResult.description: Result of a filesystem RPC call. Closed enum with `deny_unknown_fields` so a compromised agent can't smuggle extra data past the host's deserializer.

oneOf.description: Bytes read. `total_size` is the on-disk size at read time so callers can detect short reads even when `content.len() < requested length`.
Bytes successfully written.
Directory listing. `truncated` is `true` when the entry count exceeded the agent's per-call cap.
File / directory metadata.
Directory created (no payload).
Removed `entries_removed` filesystem entries (1 for a single file/dir, more under `recursive=true`).
Move / rename completed.
Verb-specific error. Distinct from `GuestResponse::Error`, which is reserved for transport-layer failures the agent can't attribute to a specific verb.

FsStat.description: Stat metadata for a single filesystem entry.

canonical_path.description: Canonical (post-`realpath`) path the agent operated on. Lets the host detect when a symlink resolution surprised it.

mode.description: Unix mode bits (e.g. `0o100644`). Always present; on backends without a unix mode the agent reports a best-effort equivalent.

mtime.description: Modification timestamp as RFC 3339, or `None` if the underlying fs doesn't expose mtime.

GuestCapability.description: Guest-agent control protocol capability. Closed enum so host and guest fail loudly on drift instead of accepting arbitrary strings.

oneOf.description: Plan 76 Phase 2 — `ReadinessStatus` returns `GuestResponse::ReadinessStatusReport(ReadinessReport)`. `mvmctl wait` / `mvmctl boot-report` require this capability.

GuestRequest.description:
Request sent from host to guest vsock agent.

`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` is load-bearing: ADR-002 §W4.1 requires the guest agent to refuse frames whose JSON contains fields the deserializer doesn't recognise, on the principle that silent acceptance of unknown fields is a deserialization-bug gadget waiting to happen. Today every variant is a struct or unit, so the attribute applies cleanly.

oneOf.description: Negotiate guest-agent protocol compatibility and capabilities before dispatching capability-dependent requests. ADR-053 / plan 74 W1.
Query current worker status.
Request sleep preparation. Guest should: 1. Finish/checkpoint in-flight OpenClaw work 2. Flush data to disk 3. Drop page cache 4. ACK with SleepPrepAck
Signal wake — guest should reinitialize connections and refresh secrets.
Health probe.
Query status of all managed integrations.
Checkpoint named integrations before sleep. Sent before SleepPrep so integrations can persist session state.
Query status of all loaded probes.
Run a command inside the guest (dev-only, requires dev-shell feature + SecurityPolicy).

Run the image's baked entrypoint program with the given stdin piped in and stdout/stderr captured. ADR-007 / plan 41 W1.

This is the production-safe call surface. The agent reads the entrypoint path from `/etc/mvm/entrypoint` at boot, validates it (verity-partition, mode, ownership), and that resolved path is the only program `RunEntrypoint` will spawn. There is no argv override, no shell, no env injection beyond what the wrapper template defines at image build time.

The response is a stream of `EntrypointEvent` frames terminated by `EntrypointEvent::Exit` or `EntrypointEvent::Error`. v1 emits one `Stdout` chunk + one `Stderr` chunk + a terminal event (buffered up to caps); v2 may chunk progressively without changing the wire shape.

Caps and timeouts are enforced agent-side (W2). The wire frame size is bounded by `MAX_FRAME_SIZE`.

env.description: Env vars injected into the workload after `env_clear()` (Plan 129: `HTTP_PROXY` + secret placeholder vars). Empty for a plain call; omitted on the wire defaults to empty.

stdin.description: Bytes piped to the wrapper's stdin.

timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock timeout for the call, in seconds. The agent kills the wrapper on overrun and emits `EntrypointEvent::Error { kind: Timeout }`.

oneOf.description: Signal post-restore: remount drives and restart services.
Request filesystem diff (changes since boot, from overlay or snapshot).
Start a vsock→TCP port forwarder for the given guest port. The agent binds vsock port `PORT_FORWARD_BASE + guest_port` and forwards each connection to `localhost:guest_port`.
Open an interactive PTY console session (dev-mode only). The guest allocates a PTY, spawns a shell, and listens on a dedicated vsock data port for raw byte streaming.
Close an active console session.
Resize the PTY window for an active console session.

Query whether the agent's boot-time entrypoint validation succeeded. Used by `mvmctl doctor` to confirm a running guest can actually serve `RunEntrypoint`. ADR-007 / plan 41 W5. Prod-safe — reveals no secrets, takes no inputs.

Query structured readiness across every guest subsystem (control plane, entrypoint, warm pool, integrations, probes, volumes) plus per-phase boot timings. Plan 76 Phase 2.

Prod-safe — the response carries no secrets and reveals only state the host already chose to provision (via image config / drop-in files). Designed to be the verb that responds first after vsock bind, so a host can begin streaming progress UX before entrypoint validation or warm-pool warmup finish.

Distinct from `EntrypointStatus` (which is entrypoint-only and returns a flat `EntrypointStatusReport`): `ReadinessStatus` reports the *full* boot phase set with `ComponentState` per component, and is intended to be polled (`mvmctl wait`).

Read up to `length` bytes from `path`, optionally starting at `offset`. The agent enforces `length` ≤ a hard cap (default 16 MiB); callers wanting larger reads must use the streaming surface (lands in W2).

follow_symlinks.description: `true` to follow symlinks during canonicalization. Default `true` for read; the host CLI may toggle to `false` for TOCTOU-resistant audits.

oneOf.description: Write `content` to `path`. Small-content path; large writes must use the streaming surface (W2).

follow_symlinks.description: Defaults to `false` for write — TOCTOU-safe default since a malicious symlink could redirect the write.

mode.description: File mode for newly-created files (e.g. `0o644`). Ignored when overwriting an existing file (existing perms kept).

oneOf.description: List entries in `path`. Cap: 4096 entries; truncated flag set in the response when exceeded.
Stat `path`. `follow_symlinks=false` returns metadata about the symlink itself (`lstat`).
Create directory at `path`. With `parents=true` the call behaves like `mkdir -p`.
Remove `path`. With `recursive=true` the call walks subtrees; the agent caps the walked-entry count to bound work.

follow_symlinks.description: Defaults to `false` for remove; symlink-following on remove is a known footgun.

oneOf.description: Rename `from` to `to`. Refuses to cross filesystem boundaries (returns `Errno::XDEV` rather than copy-then-delete).

Spawn a new process. Returns a `pid_token` string the host uses to refer to the process for the rest of its lifetime — the token is opaque to the host so a buggy or malicious caller can never address a process it didn't start.

Children spawned this way inherit the agent's bounding-set (`--bounding-set=-all --no-new-privs` per ADR-002 §W4.5); the handler additionally `process_group(0)`s and sets `RLIMIT_CORE=0` to avoid coredump exfil. argv is validated against an allowlist before exec.

argv.description: Argument vector. `argv[0]` is the executable to spawn.

cwd.description: Working directory inside the guest. `None` = process inherits the agent's cwd.

env.description: Environment variables. Replaces (does not extend) the agent's environment.

stdin.description: Initial stdin bytes. Further input goes via `ProcSendInput`.

timeout_secs.description: Optional wall-clock kill on overrun. `None` = no agent- imposed timeout; the caller can still send SIGTERM via `ProcSignal` or `ProcKill`.

oneOf.description: List processes currently tracked by the agent's PID-token map. Includes still-running and recently-exited entries until the agent reaps them (default: keep for 60 s after exit).

Send `signum` to the process named by `pid_token`. Common signals are 15 (SIGTERM) and 2 (SIGINT); for SIGKILL use the dedicated `ProcKill` verb so the audit chain captures the explicit-force semantics.
Append `bytes` to the process's stdin. Capped per call by the agent (default 1 MiB) and per process (default 16 MiB ring buffer); `ProcResult::InputAccepted` reports actual bytes written.

Wait for the process named by `pid_token` to exit, with an optional timeout. Response is a stream of `ProcWaitEvent` frames (stdout/stderr chunks) terminated by an `Exit`, `Killed`, `TimedOut`, or `Error` event.
Send SIGKILL to the process named by `pid_token`. Distinct from `ProcSignal { signum: 9 }` so the audit emit can be typed `ProcKilled` instead of a generic signal event.

Mount a virtio-fs volume inside the guest. The host has already attached the device and the agent only needs to run the in-guest mount(2) call. `volume_name` is the virtio-fs tag string the device was created with — named per plan 45 to align with the `Volume` wire type. (Replaces the former `MountShare` per plan 45 §D5.)

Unmount a previously-mounted volume. `force = false` returns `EBUSY` when the kernel reports active fds; the caller passes `force = true` to demand a lazy detach. (Replaces the former `UnmountShare` per plan 45 §D5.)

Update the warm-process pool's idle-recycle timeout. Workers that have been idle (no in-flight call) longer than `secs` are recycled at the next sweep. `secs == 0` disables idle-based recycling — only `max_calls_per_worker` and `max_rss_mb` triggers remain.

This is the substrate-side mirror of `mvmctl session set-timeout <id> <secs>`: the host writes the new value into the session record, then dispatches this verb so the agent's pool sees the same value. A best-effort dispatch — if the agent is unreachable the host record still wins on the next `mvmctl session reap`.

Run user-supplied source code in the wrapper's native interpreter. Dev-only — gated behind the agent's `dev-shell` feature flag, same fence as `Exec`. The host (`mvmctl session run-code`) provides additional gating: the session must be `mode=Dev`.

The interpreter is selected by reading `/etc/mvm/wrapper.json` at dispatch time: - `language = "python"` → `python3 -c <code>` - `language = "node"`   → `node -e <code>`

Other values, or a missing/unparseable wrapper.json, refuse with a wire-stable error message.

**v1 is stateless** — each call spawns a fresh interpreter process, so `from foo import bar` in call 1 isn't visible in call 2. A future v2 (Plan-0010 §run-code Choice A) routes through the warm-process pool's wrapper for stateful eval across calls; the wire shape stays identical, the dispatch flips inside the agent.

GuestResponse.description:
Response from guest vsock agent to host.

Same `deny_unknown_fields` discipline as `GuestRequest` — a compromised guest must not be able to slip extra fields past the host's deserializer.

oneOf.description: Guest-agent protocol negotiation succeeded. ADR-053 / plan 74 W1.
Guest-agent protocol negotiation failed before dispatch.
Worker status with optional last-busy timestamp.
Sleep preparation acknowledgement.
Wake acknowledgement.
Pong.
Error from guest agent.

The dispatcher refused this verb because the active `AgentProfile` does not allow it (plan 76 Phase 1). Distinct from `Error { message }` so SDK callers can branch on capability without parsing message text — analogous to `ProcErrorKind::UnsupportedInProduction` for process RPC, but at the protocol layer rather than per-handler.

profile.description: Active profile on the agent that rejected the call.

oneOf.description: Per-integration status report.
Result of checkpointing integrations before sleep.

failed.description: Names of integrations that failed to checkpoint.

oneOf.description: Per-probe status report.
Result of an Exec request.

One event in the response stream of a `RunEntrypoint` call. ADR-007 / plan 41 W1.

The agent emits a sequence of these in response to a single `RunEntrypoint` request, terminated by an `EntrypointEvent` whose `is_terminal` returns true (`Exit` or `Error`). The host reads frames in a loop until terminal.
Post-restore acknowledgement.
Filesystem diff result.
Port forward started successfully.
Console PTY session opened. Connect to `data_port` for raw I/O.
Console PTY session ended (shell exited).
Console resize acknowledged.

Result of an `EntrypointStatus` query. ADR-007 / plan 41 W5.

`ok = true` means the agent successfully validated `/etc/mvm/entrypoint` at boot and will serve `RunEntrypoint`. `ok = false` means validation failed — `path` carries the resolved path attempt (or the marker contents if resolution itself failed) and `detail` carries a human-readable reason.
Result of a `ReadinessStatus` query. Plan 76 Phase 2. Snapshot of every component plus per-phase timings.
Result of a filesystem RPC call. The single top-level variant keeps `GuestResponse` from sprawling — the `FsResult` sub-enum carries the per-verb shapes. W1 / A1.
Result of a non-streaming process-control verb (`ProcStart`, `ProcList`, `ProcSignal`, `ProcSendInput`, `ProcKill`). W1 / A2.

One event in the streaming response of a `ProcWait` call. Mirrors the `EntrypointEvent` shape — the agent emits `Stdout`/`Stderr` chunks (capped per chunk by the wire frame limit) terminated by exactly one of `Exit` / `Killed` / `TimedOut` / `Error`.
Result of a `MountVolume` / `UnmountVolume` call. Single-frame surface; closed sub-enum carries the per-verb shape. (Renamed from `ShareResult` per plan 45 §D5.)

Acknowledgement for `UpdateIdleTimeout`. `applied_secs` is the value the agent is now enforcing — `0` means the warm-process pool isn't active on this guest (cold-path-only build), so the host reaper is the only enforcement.

IntegrationHealthResult.description: Result of a single health check execution.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this check ran.

detail.description: Human-readable detail ("ok" on success, stderr or exit code on failure).

healthy.description: Whether the health check passed (exit code 0).

IntegrationStateReport.description: Full state report for a single integration (returned by guest agent).

health.description: Latest health check result, if a health_cmd is configured.

last_checkpoint_at.description: ISO timestamp of last successful checkpoint.

state_size_bytes.description: Bytes of state data on disk.

IntegrationStatus.description: Runtime status of a single integration on a guest.

oneOf.description: Integration is running and connected.
Integration is paused (e.g. during checkpoint).
Integration has an error.
Integration is not yet initialized.
Integration is within its startup grace period — health checks are running but failures are suppressed until the grace window expires.

ProbeResult.description: Result of running a single probe.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this probe ran.

detail.description: Human-readable detail (stderr for exit_code mode, error message on failure).

output.description: Parsed stdout JSON (only for json output_format, None otherwise).

ProcErrorKind.description: Class of error returned in `ProcResult::Error` and `ProcWaitEvent::Error`.

oneOf.description: `pid_token` doesn't match any known process. Either the host fabricated it or the agent reaped the process record.
The agent failed to spawn the child (executable missing, EACCES, ENOMEM, etc.).
Per-child seccomp / setpriv envelope failed to apply. Agent refuses to spawn an un-confined child.
argv was empty, argv\[0\] was empty / not absolute / on a disallowed path.
One or more env keys / values failed validation (charset, length).
`cwd` failed canonicalization or hit the deny-list.
Per-VM concurrent-process cap or per-call byte cap exceeded.
Returned by prod builds whose handler module was stripped per ADR-002 §W4.3. Lets SDK callers branch on capability.
Other / unclassified.

argv0.description: argv\[0\] for display only — the agent does not expose the full argv over the wire (it could echo secrets the caller passed in via env / stdin).

ProcResult.description: Result of a non-streaming process-control verb. Closed enum with `deny_unknown_fields` so a compromised agent can't smuggle extra fields past the host's deserializer.

oneOf.description: `ProcStart` succeeded — `pid_token` is the opaque handle the host uses for the rest of the process's lifetime.
`ProcList` snapshot. Order is agent-defined (typically by `started_at`).
`ProcSignal` delivered.
`ProcSendInput` accepted some/all of the bytes. `bytes_accepted` may be less than the request's `bytes.len()` if the per-process input ring buffer would overflow.
`ProcKill` issued SIGKILL.
Verb-specific error. Distinct from `GuestResponse::Error`, which is reserved for transport-layer failures.

ProcState.description: Lifecycle state of a tracked process.

oneOf.description: Process was killed by signal `i32`.
Process exceeded its `timeout_secs`; agent killed the pgroup.

ProcWaitEvent.description: One event in the streaming response of a `ProcWait` call. Terminal events end the stream — the host loops on `is_terminal()` just like for `EntrypointEvent`.

oneOf.description: Bytes from the process's stdout.
Bytes from the process's stderr.
Process exited with the given code. Terminal.
Process was killed by signal. Terminal.
`timeout_secs` elapsed; agent killed the process group. Terminal.
Agent-side condition prevented the wait (unknown token, internal failure, prod-stripped). Terminal.

A streaming resource is throttled (ADR-053 §5 / plan 74 W4). **Non-terminal.** The agent emits this on the rising edge of a backpressure condition — typically the host-side stdout/ stderr buffer crossing its high-water mark. The wait loop continues; subsequent `Stdout` / `Stderr` / terminal events signal that flow has resumed.

`detail` is a bounded, redacted human-readable hint (operator-facing). It **never** carries argv, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, or filesystem paths — see ADR-053's payload invariant.

ProtocolUpgradeAction.description: Required remediation for a host/guest protocol mismatch.

ReadinessReport.description:
Snapshot of agent readiness at the moment of a `ReadinessStatus` call.

Plan 76 Phase 2 §"Early control-plane readiness". Used by host callers (`mvmctl wait`, `mvmctl up --timings`, `mvmctl doctor`) to distinguish:

- "control plane is up, workload not yet warm" → invoke would block; the host can stream progress to the user - "entrypoint validation failed" → invoke would fail fast with a typed error; the host can surface the validation message - "optional subsystem failed" → invoke is still safe; the host surfaces a warning

`Default` composes the `Default` impls of each field — every component is `Disabled`, the profile is `SealedProd`, all timings are `None`. Tests and fixtures can construct partial reports with `..Default::default()`.

control_plane.description: Vsock listener bound and accepting. Always `Ready` if the agent could respond at all.

entrypoint.description: `/etc/mvm/entrypoint` validation result. Gates `RunEntrypoint` — a request submitted while `Starting` returns `RunEntrypointError::NotReady`.

integrations.description: Drop-in integration scan + health loop. `Disabled` if no `/etc/mvm/integrations.d/*.json` files present.

probes.description: Drop-in probe scan + probe loop. `Disabled` if no `/etc/mvm/probes.d/*.json` files present.

profile.description: Active agent profile. Same value the dispatcher uses for the `allowed_in` gate.

volumes.description: Volume-mount state — wire-stable placeholder. `Disabled` in v1 (mount/unmount are on-demand verbs, not boot state).

warm_pool.description: Warm-process pool readiness. `Disabled` for cold-tier images; `Ready` once the `after_start.sh` probe passes.

RunEntrypointError.description:
Kind of agent-side error reported via `EntrypointEvent::Error`. ADR-007 / plan 41 W1.

The variants are deliberately coarse — the host correlates by `kind` and surfaces the human-readable `message` to the operator. Adding a variant is a wire change; renaming or removing is a breaking change.

oneOf.description: Inbound stdin or buffered stdout/stderr exceeded the cap configured for the call.
The wrapper exceeded `timeout_secs`. Agent killed the process group.
Another `RunEntrypoint` is in flight on this VM. M12: agents serialize per-VM; concurrency comes from pool growth.
The wrapper process died unexpectedly (signal, OOM, etc.).

Entrypoint validation has not yet completed. Plan 76 Phase 2: the agent binds vsock early and validates entrypoint in the background, so a host that races `RunEntrypoint` ahead of `ReadinessStatus { entrypoint: Ready }` gets this back rather than `EntrypointInvalid` (which would imply a permanent failure). Hosts should poll readiness, not retry blindly.

`/etc/mvm/entrypoint` is missing, fails validation (symlink crossing FS, wrong perms, off the verity partition), or otherwise can't be loaded. Reported per-call even though the validation runs at agent boot.

The session backing this call was killed externally (host invoked `mvmctl session kill <id>`) while the call was in flight. Synthesized host-side by `mvmctl invoke` / `session attach` after detecting a transport-level connection drop coincident with a session record marked `Killed`. The agent itself does not emit this — it would be torn down with the VM before it could.
Other agent-internal failure — file I/O, vsock framing, inter-process plumbing. Look at `message` for detail.

VolumeMountErrorKind.description: Class of error returned in `VolumeMountResult::Error`. Closed enum so the host can branch on `kind` without parsing message text. (Renamed from `ShareErrorKind` per plan 45 §D5.)

oneOf.description: `guest_path` is empty / not absolute / contains `..` / embedded NUL.
`guest_path` resolved to a deny-prefix or fell outside the allow-roots configured for this image.
`volume_name` is empty, too long, or contains characters virtio-fs won't accept as a tag.
`mount(2)` returned a non-EBUSY error (no virtiofsd, kernel missing virtio_fs module, etc.).
`umount(2)` returned EBUSY and `force = false` — caller must retry with `force = true` to lazy-detach.
Underlying I/O error not mapped above.
Any other unclassified failure.

oneOf.description: `MountVolume` succeeded. `canonical_path` is the post-validation path the agent actually mounted at — same shape as input but with trailing slashes normalised.
`UnmountVolume` succeeded.
Verb-specific error.
